source_text: ριε, εἰ ἄρα εὗρον χάριν ἐναντίον σου, μὴ παρέλθῃς τὸν παῖδά σου· ληφθήτω δὴ ὕδωρ, καὶ νιψάτωσαν τοὺς πόδας ὑμῶν, καὶ καταψύξατε ὑπὸ τὸ δένδρον, καὶ λήψομαι ἄρτον, καὶ φάγεσθε, καὶ μετὰ τοῦτο παρελεύσεσθε εἰς τὴν ὁδὸν ὑμῶν, οὗ ἕνεκεν ἐξεκλίνατε πρὸς τὸν παῖδα ὑμῶν. Καὶ εἶπον· Οὕτω ποιήσομεν, καθὼς εἴρηκας.» Ἡ μὲν γὰρ ἐν σαρκὶ περιτομὴ, τύπος ἂν εἴη καὶ μάλα σαφὴς, τῆς νοητῆς καὶ ἐν πνεύματι, καθ' ἣν ἅπαντα μολυσμὸν τῶν ἡμετέρων διανοιῶν ἐξίστησιν ὁ Χριστός. «Περιτετμήμεθα γὰρ, κατά γε τὴν τοῦ μακαρίου Παύλου φωνὴν, περιτομῇ ἀχειροποιήτῳ ἐν τῇ ἀπεκδύσει τῆς σαρκός.» Ἀπημφιεσμένοι γὰρ ὥσπερ τὸν παλαιὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν φθειρόμενον κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς ἀπάτης, καὶ τὰς τῆς σαρκὸς ἡδονὰς τῇ τοῦ πνεύματος ὀξύτητί τε καὶ ἐνεργείᾳ μονονουχὶ παρακεκομμένοι, ἀξίους ἑαυτοὺς ἀποφανοῦμεν ἤδη πως τοῦ καὶ θεοπτίας ἀξιοῦσθαι δεῖν, καὶ ἱερὸν γενέσθαι κατάλυμα τῆς ἁγίας τε καὶ ὁμοουσίου Τριάδος. «Ὃς γὰρ ἂν ἐπαισχυνθῇ με καὶ τοὺς ἐμοὺς λόγους ἐν τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ, ἐλευσόμεθα ἐγὼ καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ, καὶ μονὴν παρ' αὐτῷ ποιησόμεθα, καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ καταλύσομεν,» ἔφασκεν ὁ Σωτήρ. Καὶ οὐ μέχρι τούτων, τῆς ἐπιεικείας ἡ ἀντέκτισις, ἀλλ' ὡς ἤδη παραδεχθέντες πρὸς οἰκειότητα τὴν ὡς πρὸς Θεὸν, τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ γνωσόμεθα, δι' ἀποκαλύψεως δὲ δηλονότι τῆς παρ' αὐτῷ· καθάπερ ἀμέλει καὶ ὁ θεσπέσιος Ἀβραὰμ τὰ περὶ τῆς τῶν Σοδόμων καταστροφῆς ἐδιδάσκετο. Φίλῳ γὰρ ὥσπερ ἀνεκοινοῦτο Θεός. Ἄθρει δὴ οὖν ὅτι μυρίων ὅσων ἡμῖν ἀγαθῶν ἐμποιήσειεν ἀντέκτισιν, τὸ ἐξοίχεσθαι μολυσμῶν. Τοιγάρτοι καὶ Παῦλος, «Παρακαλῶ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοὶ,» φησὶ, «διὰ τῶν οἰκτιρμῶν τοῦ Θεοῦ, παραστῆσαι τὰ σώματα ὑμῶν θυσίαν ζῶσαν, ἁγίαν, εὐάρεστον τῷ Θεῷ, τὴν λογικὴν λατρείαν ὑμῶν.» Καὶ μὴν καὶ ὁ προφήτης Ἱερεμίας ἀνακέκραγε σαφῶς· «Ἀπόπλυνε ἀπὸ κακίας τὴν καρδίαν, Ἱερουσαλὴμ, ἵνα σωθῇς.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Προσιτέον δὴ οὖν οὐκ ἐν βεβηλώσει ψυχῆς τῷ παναγίῳ Θεῷ, ἀλλ' ὡς ἐν ἱερᾷ τε καὶ ἀμωμήτῳ ζωῇ. Κατ' εὐθὺ γὰρ ὧδε τοῦ πρέποντος ἥξομεν. {ΚΥΡ.} Πάνυ μὲν οὖν, ὦ Παλλάδιε, καὶ οὐ πολλοῦ τε, οἶμαι, δεήσει πόνου πρὸς τὸ δύνασθαι καταθρεῖν ἀληθῶς ἔχοντά σοι τὸν ἐπὶ τῷδε λόγον, εἰ τὰς τῶν ἁγίων πολυτείας πολυπραγμονεῖν ἕλοιο φιλομαθῶς καὶ ὁμοφρόνως· τὰ γὰρ τοῖς ἀρχαίοις συμβεβηκότα τυπικῶς, νουθεσίας ἡμῖν ἔφασκεν ἀναγεγράφθαι τρόπους ὁ θεσπέσιος Παῦλος. Οὐκοῦν ὅτι καθαροὺς καὶ ἐκνενιμμένους προσιέναι δεῖ τῷ Θεῷ, διαμάθοι τις ἂν κἀκ τῶνδε δὴ πάλιν. Δῖνα μὲν γὰρ ἡ ἐξ Ἰακὼβ, ἅτε παρθένος καὶ ἐν ὤρᾳ γάμου, τὰς τῶν ἐν Σικίμοις θυγατέρας κατοπτεύουσα, τῆς πατρῴας ἐξέθει σκηνῆς, ἀλλ' οὐκ ἠρέμει Συχὲμ ὁ Ἐμμὼρ υἱός. Ἐρᾷ γὰρ εὐθὺς τῆς νεάνιδος, καὶ ἀσχέτοις ἐπιθυμίαις ἐπὶ τὸ δοκοῦν ἡρπάζετο. Ἀγροικότερον δὲ πρὸς τοῦτο ἰὼν, κατεβιάζετο τὴν παρθένον τὴν Ἑβραίαν ὁ ἀλλόφυλός τε καὶ ἀπερίτμητος ἔτι. Δύσοιστον δὲ τὸ χρῆμα ἐδόκει τοῖς ἐξ Ἰακὼβ, καὶ τοῖς ἀνοσίως πεπαρῳνηκόσιν εἰς Ἑβραίαν καὶ ἀδελφὴν, τὸν πολέμου νόμον ἐπῄεσαν. Ἀσχάλλοντα δὲ καὶ περιδεῆ γεγονότα τὸν θεσπέσιον Ἰακὼβ, καὶ ἐν ὑποψίαις ὄντα τοῦ διόλ
pass_a_gloss: [Gen 18:3-5 cont.] Lord, if I found grace before you, do not pass by your servant; let water be taken and let them wash your feet, and cool/rest under the tree, and I will take bread and you will eat, and after this you will pass on your way, for which reason you turned aside to your servant. And they said: Thus we will do, as you said. For the circumcision in flesh would be a type, very clear, of the intelligible/inward one in spirit, by which Christ removes every defilement of our thoughts. For we have been circumcised, by blessed Paul's voice, with circumcision not-made-by-hands in the putting off of the flesh (Col 2:11). For having stripped off as it were the old man corrupted according to the desires of deceit (Eph 4:22), and all but cut away the pleasures of the flesh by the sharpness and working of the spirit/Spirit, we will show ourselves worthy already somehow of being deemed worthy of God-seeing, and to become a holy lodging of the holy and consubstantial Trinity. 'For whoever is ashamed of me and my words in this generation, we will come, I and the Father, and make abode with him and lodge in him,' said the Savior. And not up to these is the repayment of goodness/fairness, but as already received to closeness toward God we will know the things in him, through revelation from him; as divine Abraham was taught about the overthrow of Sodom. For God communicated as to a friend. See that to be quit of defilements would produce repayment of countless goods. Paul: I exhort you, brothers, by the compassions of God, to present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, well-pleasing to God, your rational worship (Rom 12:1). Jeremiah cried clearly: Wash off from wickedness your heart, Jerusalem, that you may be saved (Jer 4:14). PALL: One must approach the all-holy God not in profanation of soul, but as in holy and blameless life; thus we will come straight to the fitting. CYR: Certainly, Palladius; it will need not much labor to behold the account on this as truly holding, if you choose to busy yourself with the conduct of the saints learning-lovingly and like-mindedly; for what happened typically to the ancients was written as modes of admonition, said divine Paul (1 Cor 10:11). So that pure and washed one must approach God one may learn from these too. Dinah from Jacob, a virgin in the season of marriage, spying on the daughters of those in Shechem, ran out of the paternal tent; but Shechem son of Hamor was not quiet. He loves the girl at once and was snatched by unrestrained desires toward what seemed good. Going at it rather boorishly, the foreigner and still uncircumcised forced the Hebrew virgin. Unbearable the thing seemed to those from Jacob, and on those who unholily outraged a Hebrew and sister they brought the law of war. Divine Jacob, vexed and very fearful and in suspicion of being utterly destroyed [continues in 30].
pass_b_english: Cyril: ‘…Lord, if indeed I have found favor before you, do not pass by your servant. Let water be brought, and let them wash your feet, and refresh yourselves under the tree; and I will bring bread, and you shall eat; and after this you shall go on your way, since it is for this that you have turned aside to your servant. And they said: We will do so, as you have said’ (Genesis 18:3–5).

For circumcision in the flesh would be a very clear type of the inward circumcision, the circumcision in the spirit (Romans 2:29), by which Christ removes all defilement from our thoughts. For, in the words of the blessed Paul, ‘we have been circumcised with a circumcision made without hands, in the putting off of the flesh’ (Colossians 2:11). For when we have, as it were, stripped off the old self, which is being corrupted by deceitful desires (Ephesians 4:22), and have all but cut away the pleasures of the flesh by the keen edge and the working of the Spirit, we shall already, in some measure, show ourselves fit to be counted worthy even of seeing God, and of becoming a sacred dwelling place of the holy and consubstantial Trinity. ‘For whoever is ashamed of me and of my words in this generation, we will come, I and the Father, and make our home with him, and dwell in him,’ said the Savior (Mark 8:38; John 14:23).

Nor does the reward of goodness stop there. Rather, as those already received into close fellowship with God, we shall come to know the things that are in him, through the revelation that comes from him, of course; just as the divine Abraham too was taught about the overthrow of Sodom (Genesis 18:17–21). For God shared his counsel with him as with a friend. See, then, that to be rid of defilements would bring us in return countless good things. Therefore Paul too says: ‘I appeal to you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy, well pleasing to God, which is your reasonable worship’ (Romans 12:1). And indeed the prophet Jeremiah cried out plainly: ‘Wash your heart clean of wickedness, Jerusalem, that you may be saved’ (Jeremiah 4:14).
Palladius: We must approach the all-holy God, then, not with a profaned soul, but in a holy and blameless life. For in this way we shall go straight to what is fitting.

Cyril: Quite so, Palladius. And I think it will take you no great labor to see that what is said on this point holds true, if you choose to search into the lives of the saints with a love of learning and with a mind that agrees with mine. For the divine Paul said that the things that befell those of old as types were written down as a way of admonishing us (1 Corinthians 10:11). That we must approach God pure and washed, then, one could learn once more from the following as well. For Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, being a virgin and of an age for marriage, ran out of her father’s tent to look at the daughters of the people of Shechem (Genesis 34:1). But Shechem, the son of Hamor, did not keep still. He at once fell in love with the girl (Genesis 34:3) and was swept away by unrestrained desires toward what he had set his mind on. Going about it rather brutishly, the foreigner, who was still uncircumcised, forced the Hebrew virgin (Genesis 34:2). The sons of Jacob found the matter unbearable (Genesis 34:7), and by the law of war they fell upon those who had impiously outraged a Hebrew woman, their own sister (Genesis 34:25–29). As for the divine Jacob, who was distressed and terrified, and who feared that he would be utterly destroyed…

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De adoratione Book 14 exists to compare. Translated fresh from the Migne PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withheld earlier English was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: Migne PG 68 print; the column break may cut a sentence or a word.

DOUBTFUL READING (needs editorial decision): the Savior's saying is printed as 'Ὃς γὰρ ἂν ἐπαισχυνθῇ με καὶ τοὺς ἐμοὺς λόγους ἐν τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ, ἐλευσόμεθα ἐγὼ καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ, καὶ μονὴν παρ' αὐτῷ ποιησόμεθα, καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ καταλύσομεν.' The opening clause is Mark 8:38 ('whoever is ashamed of me and my words in this generation'), which contradicts the promise that follows; the promise is John 14:23 ('if anyone loves me he will keep my word ... we will come to him and make our home with him'), with an added 'and dwell in him'. Both the Migne PDF text and the cleaned text read the same, so this is the printed text, not an OCR slip; Cyril's argument needs John 14:23, and the print may have lost or garbled the conditional. Translated exactly as printed, with both references cited; consider a note or a check of the critical text before publishing. Genesis 18:5 reply: the source reads ποιήσομεν ('we will do'), LXX ποίησον ('do'); translated as printed. Colossians 2:11 is quoted in shortened form (LXX/NT 'the body of the flesh' becomes 'the flesh'). 'τοῦ πνεύματος' in 'keenness and working of the Spirit' could mean the human spirit set against the flesh; capitalized as the Holy Spirit, which suits Cyril's usage, but this is a judgment. 'Inward circumcision ... in the spirit' (νοητῆς καὶ ἐν πνεύματι) is cited to Romans 2:29 by the reviewer as a clear Pauline allusion (circumcision of the heart, in the spirit). 'God shared His counsel with him as with a friend' may echo Abraham as 'friend of God' (Isaiah 41:8; James 2:23); left uncited. Sodom revelation cited to Genesis 18:17–21 (God's disclosure to Abraham). λογικὴν λατρείαν rendered 'reasonable worship' to keep λατρεία = worship, the title word of the work. πολυτείας is read as πολιτείας ('lives, conduct'). The Dinah narrative is Cyril's paraphrase of Genesis 34, not a quotation; citations mark the verses paraphrased. ὁμοφρόνως rendered 'with a mind that agrees with mine' (or 'in a like spirit'). The last sentence runs on across the section break (διόλ|λυσθαι); the main clause 'God received him' opens section 30.
Genesis 18:3–5 continuation: removed stray inner quote marks so the run-on quotation from section 28 closes once, matching the colon style used in Genesis 17 and 34
Added Romans 2:29 for circumcision 'in the spirit'
Ephesians 4:22: 'is being corrupted by deceitful desires' (present participle, natural order)
ἤδη πως: 'already, in some measure', not 'at last'; ἱερόν as 'sacred' to avoid 'holy ... holy'; ὀξύτης as 'keen edge' (blade image of circumcision)
τῶνδε: 'from the following'; ἐξέθει: 'ran out'; restored connective 'For'

Dinah citations split: love = Genesis 34:3, force = Genesis 34:2; added Genesis 34:7 for the brothers' anger; ἀνοσίως 'impiously' without added 'so'; 'brought the law of war' recast as 'by the law of war they fell upon'

OWNER: the Savior's saying is printed as Mark 8:38 ('whoever is ashamed of Me') joined to the John 14:23 promise ('we will come ... make Our home with him'), which reads as a contradiction in English; translated as printed, needs a check of the critical text (a lost μή or lost clause) before publishing
